function: p. 1: Generative adversarial network (MIA-GAN) estimates the uplink channel matrix of a massive MIMO system from one-bit quantized pilot observations, targeting inadequate training samples.
system: p. 3: Uplink massive MIMO, BS with M antennas, single-antenna users, K=32 subcarriers, one-bit ADCs; M=64-256, 2.4 GHz, 0.01 GHz bandwidth (Table I, p. 7); no RIS.
method: p. 4: GAN with modified U-Net generator (Pooling Fusion, SE-DSC) and Pyramid DConv discriminator; supervised adversarial training on quantized-signal and true-channel pairs, GAN plus Huber loss.
data_channel: p. 7: DeepMIMO ray-tracing dataset (Remcom Wireless InSite), indoor scenario I1_2p4, N=2211 users, L=10 paths, K=32 subcarriers, M=64-256 antennas (Table I), 2.4 GHz.
test_conditions: p. 8: Per condition, 2211 samples split 8:2 (adequate) or 2:8 (limited, p. 9) into training and test sets; SNR, antenna and pilot-length sweeps; one indoor scenario only.
baselines: p. 8: Non-learned: GAMP-Laplace (compressive sensing); learned: DI-DNN, SF-CNN, A-Deep CNN, ResNet-UNet, cGAN; plus loss-function comparison (Huber, smooth L1, log-Cosh, L1, L2).
metrics: p. 7: NMSE (dB) versus SNR, number of samples, BS antennas, pilot length and loss; convergence curves; model size (million parameters) and billion FLOPs (p. 10).
complexity: p. 10: Table III: MIA-GAN 17.2883 million parameters and 10.0862 billion FLOPs; compared with cGAN, ResNet-UNet, SF-CNN, DI-DNN and A-Deep CNN.
openness: p. 1: Code of MIA-GAN at https://github.com/luanshengyang/MIA-GAN; DeepMIMO public dataset (scenario I1_2p4).
q1_support: p. 7: "generate the DeepMIMO dataset [38] for performance evaluation" - DeepMIMO ray tracing (Remcom Wireless InSite, scenario I1_2p4) is used for both training and testing.
q2_support: p. 8: "a training set and a test set at 8:2 to ensure sufficient samples for" - test samples are held out from the same DeepMIMO scenario under each condition; p. 7 says layer dimensions change with the condition, and transfer learning and domain adaptation appear only as future work (p. 11).
q3_support: p. 8: "Seven methods are included in the experiments to exhibit the" - non-learned GAMP-Laplace [11] and learned DI-DNN, SF-CNN, A-Deep CNN, ResNet-UNet and cGAN [14] are compared on NMSE (Figs. 9-13).
q4_support: p. 10: "MODEL SIZES AND COMPUTATIONAL COMPLEXITIES" - Table III gives MIA-GAN 17.2883 million parameters and 10.0862 billion FLOPs; p. 11: "while its computational complexity is about one-eighth of" ResNet-UNet.
q5_support: p. 1: "The codes of MIA-GAN and individual substructures are shared at" - link https://github.com/luanshengyang/MIA-GAN in the first-page footnote; p. 7 also uses the public DeepMIMO dataset.
notes: Included, area 2: channel estimation for one-bit massive MIMO. q1 and q5 rest on DeepMIMO (scenario I1_2p4) and on the GitHub link in the first-page footnote; p. 7 says the code is at the link in the abstract, but the link sits in the footnote. q2=0: one indoor scenario, held-out split, no unseen condition or adaptation tested.
